scenario: AITA for being uncomfortable when my boyfriend speaks Spanish to his family around me? | I’m very rarely with my boyfriend and his family, but the few times I have been, they’d only communicate with one another through Spanish, which is a language I hardly know at all. His whole family speaks English as well, but they choose to speak Spanish to one another around me, which makes me uncomfortable because a lot of times it’s regarding plans we’ve made and then my boyfriend has to turn to me and translate what they’ve all been saying, and often he leaves things out and forgets to tell me those necessary details until later. Now of course I don’t mind if it’s like, his siblings to his mother in a conversation that shouldn’t involve me, but when they’re talking with my boyfriend as he’s sitting right next to me, I just feel weird. I understand it’s their “normal language” as my boyfriend calls it, and I’m not trying to be all up in the business or try to have them change their ways, it just makes me feel left out and extremely confused and even a little awkward... I’ve mentioned it to him and he gets defensive and angry, like they’re not going to change to make me more comfortable. I just feel that if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak to me in a language my boyfriend would understand so he wouldn’t feel left out or like he’s missing something important. Before anyone tells me to simply learn Spanish, first of all, it’s not that easy and second, I am learning Spanish...trying to at least... I feel like I AM the asshole but I don’t want to be...so someone just tell me, am I the asshole?

His whole family speaks English as well, but they choose to speak Spanish to one another around me, which makes me uncomfortable because a lot of times it’s regarding plans we’ve made and then my boyfriend has to turn to me and translate what they’ve all been saying, and often he leaves things out and forgets to tell me those necessary details until later. Now of course I don’t mind if it’s like, his siblings to his mother in a conversation that shouldn’t involve me, but when they’re talking with my boyfriend as he’s sitting right next to me, I just feel weird. I understand it’s their “normal language” as my boyfriend calls it, and I’m not trying to be all up in the business or try to have them change their ways, it just makes me feel left out and extremely confused and even a little awkward... I’ve mentioned it to him and he gets defensive and angry, like they’re not going to change to make me more comfortable. I just feel that if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak to me in a language my boyfriend would understand so he wouldn’t feel left out or like he’s missing something important. Before anyone tells me to simply learn Spanish, first of all, it’s not that easy and second, I am learning Spanish...trying to at least... I feel like I AM the asshole but I don’t want to be...so someone just tell me, am I the asshole?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **0 (Not the asshole)** **Here's why:** - **Inclusion matters in shared spaces:** When a conversation *directly involves you* (e.g., plans you’re part of, decisions affecting you), it’s considerate to communicate in a language everyone understands. Excluding you intentionally (even if unintentional) creates unnecessary barriers and makes you feel like an outsider in your own relationship. - **Your request is reasonable:** You’re not asking them to *stop speaking Spanish* altogether (which would be unfair to their culture). You’re asking for basic courtesy when *you’re present and involved*. This is no different than expecting a group to switch to English if *you* were speaking a language your boyfriend didn’t know during a shared activity. - **His defensiveness is the real issue:** His reaction ("they’re not going to change for you") dismisses your feelings and prioritizes his family’s habits over your emotional comfort. A healthy relationship requires mutual respect and adaptation—not one person always "sacrificing" while the other stays rigid. - **Learning a language ≠ a solution to exclusion:** While it’s great you’re learning Spanish, *expecting you to fluently understand complex conversations on the spot is unrealistic*. This isn’t about your effort—it’s about * their* willingness to include you in *your* shared life. **What to do next:** - **Frame it as "we" language:** "I feel left out when we’re discussing plans and I can’t follow. Can we switch to English when I’m part of the conversation? It would help me feel included in * our* life together." - **Set boundaries:** If they consistently exclude you, it’s okay to say, "I need to step out if we’re talking about things I’m involved in but I can’t understand." - **Evaluate his willingness to change:** If he *never* advocates for you or dismisses your feelings long-term, this is a red flag about how he values your place in his life. **You’re not the problem here.** The issue is a lack of mutual effort to bridge the gap. Culture is important, but so is feeling respected in your own relationship. 💛 *(P.S. If you’d like help practicing Spanish or brainstorming phrases to communicate this gently, I’m here!)*
